question: A patient presents with bilateral nasal obstruction and pale, grape-like masses arising from the middle meatus. Which statement about the laterality of this condition is correct?

answers.text: Ethmoidal polyps are typically unilateral and antrochoanal polyps are typically bilateral.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: This is the reverse of the correct relationship. Antrochoanal polyps classically arise from the maxillary antrum and are unilateral; ethmoidal polyps arise from the ethmoid sinuses and are bilateral.

answers.text: Both ethmoidal and antrochoanal polyps are always bilateral.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. Antrochoanal polyps are characteristically unilateral — a key distinguishing feature from ethmoidal polyps.

answers.text: Ethmoidal polyps are typically bilateral and antrochoanal polyps are typically unilateral.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. Ethmoidal (allergic) polyps arise from both ethmoid complexes and are bilateral; antrochoanal polyps arise from a single maxillary sinus and are unilateral. Laterality is a key diagnostic differentiator.

answers.text: Both ethmoidal and antrochoanal polyps are always unilateral.

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Ethmoidal polyps are bilateral, not unilateral. Only antrochoanal polyps are characteristically unilateral.

overallFeedback.feedback: Remember: ethmoidal polyps are bilateral (arising from both ethmoid complexes in allergic disease), whereas antrochoanal polyps are unilateral (arising from one maxillary antrum). Laterality is the key differentiator.
Excellent. Bilateral nasal polyps = ethmoidal (allergic); unilateral nasal polyp = antrochoanal (maxillary antrum origin). This laterality rule is frequently tested in ENT.
